title: Portable compiler source provenance
objective: Emit portable logical Sage.js source filenames in self-hosted compiler and distributable standalone builds while preserving physical file, diagnostic, import, and cache authority

oracles: Physical and logical filename split with cache-policy and outside-root regression tests
Byte-identical fixture output across distinct physical roots and no physical-root bytes in built compiler/runtime artifacts

handoff.summary: Introduces a canonical physical/logical filename split for compiler modules. Physical paths remain authoritative for source I/O, imports, diagnostics, and cache locations, while logical src/... paths feed AST/token provenance and emitted Python module metadata. Portable cache records bind the logical filename policy; null-policy precompiled caches remain relocatable and are rehydrated with the current physical filename. Self-hosted compiler/runtime builds opt into portable identities, and the CLI exposes a fail-closed distributable-build flag. Focused tests cover relocated and conflicting cache policies, main and imported metadata/diagnostics, outside-root and symlink escape rejection, cross-platform prefix validation, CLI stdin and relative-file identity, two-root output equality, and built compiler/runtime artifacts.
risks: The fresh worktree has no FLINT addon or headers, so pnpm test:compiler and the broad integration/CLI tier reach existing native-dependent tests but fail only on the missing packages/flint/build/Release/sagejs_flint.node or flint/flint.h. The focused suite, full self build, TypeScript check, Python formatting check, and architecture audit pass.

scripts/build-runtime-cache.cjs is integration-owned. It still constructs the absolute compiler source filename before V8 cache serialization, which causes exactly one checkout-root occurrence in dist/runtime-cache/compiler.bin even though compiler.js is clean. A reproduced fix is to read/cache the compiler under a relative path without ever constructing that absolute filename.

Windows and two-root full release builds remain required after integration; this lane proves two-root equality for representative compiler output and scans its owned compiler/runtime artifacts on Linux.
next_steps: In the release integration lane, opt scripts/build-task-runtime.cjs into --portable-sagejs-paths with an explicit virtual physical filename beneath src.

In the release integration lane, make scripts/build-runtime-cache.cjs create the compiler V8 cache from a relative source filename and extend the artifact regression to compiler.bin and the task runtime.

Register test/portable-source-paths.cjs in test/node-test-manifest.cjs, rebuild, and run the full Windows release proof from two fresh checkout roots after the separately gated native path-remapping work.
